obligations.description: Daily rate is monthly_price divided by days_in_month
obligations.evidence_rationale: The candidate test asserts prorate(30,15,30)==15.0, but the plausible defect (a hard-coded price/30) gives the same answer for a 30-day month, so that mapped mutant survives - a present, relevant test that kills zero mapped mutants for this rule.

obligations.description: Charge for the days used at the daily rate
obligations.evidence_rationale: A mutant that ignores days_used gives 30 not 15, so the test kills it; but boundaries (0 days, a full month) are untested, so those mutants survive - kills some, misses some.

obligations.description: Round the result to two decimals
obligations.evidence_rationale: The candidate test exercises prorate (covering the round() call) but its asserted result (15.0) is a whole number, so a mutant that changes the rounding survives it. A present, relevant test that kills zero mapped mutants.

gaps.description: The only test uses a 30-day month, where price/days_in_month and a hard-coded price/30 give the same answer, so it cannot establish that the rate uses days_in_month
The asserted result (15.0) is a whole number, so rounding to two decimals is never exercised; a wrong rounding rule would pass
Only one input (15 of 30 days) is exercised, with no boundaries (0 days, a full month), so a violation at those boundaries would pass - partial coverage, acceptance only with that caveat
